# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis inspects the trained NextItNet through its compatibility interface; backbone implementation details are not supplied. Relevant hooks are `item_emb.weight`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. Candidate auditing left-pads each training prefix and reads features at its final nonpadding position. Margin probes instead score every supported sequence position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` receives the actual network as `view.model`, mapped training histories/timestamps, metadata and compatibility hooks. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` takes at most four batches, capped at 32 rows each, containing matching B × L sequence/positive/negative tensors. It runs without gradients in evaluation mode and restores module modes and Python, NumPy and Torch RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding geometry:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding catalog embeddings and maps mean off-diagonal cosine to [0,1]. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; 0.5 means mean cosine zero, not a collapse probability.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Reports mean and tenth-percentile score margins, negative-beats-positive rate and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and fewer reversals suggest stronger training separation, but margins depend on score scale. Padding, missing targets and nonfinite comparisons are excluded and counted.
- **Candidate stress audit:** Selects up to 200 training users and five prefixes/user. Four frozen conditions provide 99 unique competitors: uniform, frequency^0.75, prefix lexical and target lexical oracle. Reports rank, hit10, reciprocal rank, strongest-competitor margin, later-training-positive overlap and fallback fraction. Draws average within prefixes, then users; results include history-length/frequency strata and paired user-bootstrap intervals.
- **Catalog calibration:** Up to 40 prespecified user examples receive exact catalog ranking and analytic versus empirical uniform-sampling calibration.

# Perturbation & Tests

Histories remain unchanged; competitor distributions change around identical prefixes and targets. This tests ranking sensitivity to candidate difficulty. Lexical competitors use public title/description TF-IDF; target-conditioned retrieval is explicitly an oracle. Candidate selection is frozen before scoring, with hashes and trial-local artifacts.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

Output contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics include embedding/margin summaries, support, category-breakdown availability, `training_candidate_stress_audit`, and explicit unavailable validation/reload-parity entries. The interpreter prompt requests evidence-grounded status, findings, implications and headline metrics.

Training targets may be memorized; unobserved competitors are not verified negatives. No sequence-order perturbations, gradients, causal intent, unavailable traits/reviews/categories, predictor reload parity or pinned validation HR@10 are measured. Four-category macro aggregation is unavailable per invocation; null means unavailable.
